comments.body: `containsAny` is matched with `.every(...)`, which means "contains all". The server runs `containsAny` as `col::text[] && ARRAY[...]` (`compute-where-condition-parts.ts`), which means "contains at least one". `computeViewRecordGqlOperationFilter.ts:~620` sends every selected option in `containsAny`. Suppose a user filters a multi-select field for Contains [A, B], and a record with only [A] is created or updated. The server returns it, but this client-side matcher returns false. `isRecordMatchingFilter` is used by the optimistic effects (`triggerCreateRecordsOptimisticEffect.ts:90`, `triggerUpdateRecordOptimisticEffect.ts:68`), so the cache drops or omits records that should be in the list. Use `.some`.

The client builds `containsIlike` as `` `%${filter.value}%` `` (`computeViewRecordGqlOperationFilter.ts:~695`), which is an SQL ILIKE pattern. This matcher lowercases that string and checks `item.toLowerCase().includes(searchTerm)`, so it looks for the literal `%foo%`, including the percent signs. It never matches, and `Contains` filters on ARRAY fields give wrong optimistic-cache results: newly created or updated records that match the filter are excluded. Strip the `%` wildcards, or translate the pattern, before comparing.
